{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZg2XhA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDH6No", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 103, "title": "Add an evidence-qualified browser-local Gopher browsing and search journey", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `0da2372dcb7640898f990b8e5d8914203bf301a6`, MAIN or index → `7` displays NetNews, TELNET and FTP. There is no Gopher destination. Users cannot experience its characteristic progression through directories, text documents and search-result menus.

The 1996 capability comparison supports PC-VAN Gopher availability, but does not authenticate a text-host menu or command sequence. Implement a disclosed reconstruction at the tolerance accepted for neighboring local Internet services.

## Expected outcome

Add `4 Gopher` to the existing Internet directory, preserving selectors 1–3 and MAIN mappings. Provide two complete keyboard journeys:

- Internet directory → Gopher root → nested directory → original Japanese text → return through the actual entry path.
- Gopher menu → search item → query → selectable results → text → return to the same results and query; also support an honest zero-result case.

Use a small bundled corpus. Keep the experience available anonymously without AI consent or model loading.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction judgment

Sources were inspected on 2026-10-24:

- [Internet White Paper 1996, printed p.111](https://iwparchives.jp/files/pdf/iwp1996/iwp1996-ch04-01-p110.pdf): the table labeled January 1996 marks Gopher available for PC-VAN and separately lists Navigator, Mosaic and WorldTALK. Moderate-to-high confidence in reported capability. It establishes neither the original route nor text-host controls; the table also includes later planned changes, so its date is not an activation date.
- [Internet Magazine, January 1996, printed p.229](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199601-216-news.pdf): describes Navigator launching Mosaic and restrictions on choosing Internet software and Archie servers in that environment. High confidence in the inspected review’s contents. This client-specific account prevents treating capability marks as proof of independent terminal access; it does not establish a service-wide Gopher prohibition.
- [RFC 1436, March 1993](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1436.html): establishes hierarchical directories, text documents, distinct search items and searches returning selectable menus. High confidence in these Gopher semantics; it supplies no PC-VAN commands or Japanese layout.
- [Internet White Paper 1996, printed p.14](https://iwparchives.jp/files/pdf/iwp1996/iwp1996-ch01-01-p014.pdf): contemporary Japanese explanation corroborates menu-based information searching and retrieval. This is general Gopher context, not a PC-VAN manual.
- [Internet White Paper 1997, printed p.29](https://iwparchives.jp/files/pdf/iwp1997/iwp1997-ch01-06-p028.pdf): the later combined BIGLOBE comparison again marks Gopher available. This provides limited continuity context, not proof of November 1996 text-host access.

Accept category D reconstruction for Internet selector `4`, all controls, layout, Japanese labels, corpus organization and matching behavior. Carrying the capability into the fictional late-1996 setting is an explicit moderate-confidence inference. The original host/client access path remains unknown. Do not introduce `J GOPHER` or claim any proposed command was historically authenticated.

### Current implementation and integration

`src/netnews.ts::renderInternetDirectory` and `src/navigation.ts` currently expose three Internet services. Navigation already owns screen-scoped commands and contextual returns. Its document/list handling provides precedents, but Gopher documents must return to their opening directory or search results rather than always to a canonical folder.

Inspect `src/commands.ts` alongside navigation: generic WRITE/REPLY handling can otherwise intercept unsupported service input. `src/connection.ts` forwards controller state. Reuse the existing literal terminal rendering, IME guards, modern Settings/About and production Playwright infrastructure.

[PR #102](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/102) and `docs/validation.md` report 367 passing checks with three workers for the preceding increment. These are Coordinator records, not checks executed by this research graph. Default/eight-worker reliability remains unresolved.

Live repository searches found no open Issues or PRs and no Gopher/Archie Issue matches. Searches are terminology-dependent and inventory can change.

## Pre-merge acceptance

1. **Complete bounded service.** Add `4 Gopher` from both MAIN → 7 and index → 7. Bundle a root menu, at least one nested directory, at least two original Japanese text documents and one search item. Distinguish directory, text and search entries with concise user-facing labels. Use original fictional content; copy no archived messages, identities, screenshots or software.

2. **Predictable navigation.** Numbered selection operates only on the displayed menu/results. `HELP` redisplays the current view. From a document, `BACK` and `LIST` restore its opening directory or exact search results, including query and ordering. From results, `BACK` returns to the search view; further returns reach its containing menu, Gopher root, Internet directory and actual MAIN/index parent. `MAIN` clears the path. Fresh entry starts at the root without a previous query. Repeated document selection must not accumulate duplicate return frames.

3. **Small explicit search subset.** Selecting the search item opens guidance for `SEARCH <query>`. Search only the bundled document titles/bodies using deterministic, case-insensitive literal substring matching. Trim outer query whitespace while preserving internal whitespace and Japanese text. Empty/malformed queries preserve the view with useful guidance. Show the query, result count and selectable matching documents; unmatched queries yield zero results. Regex/Boolean-looking input is literal. Clearly document this matching rule as reconstruction.

4. **Command isolation and lifecycle.** Reject invalid/out-of-range selectors and unrelated forum, mail, OLT, conference, TELNET, FTP, BiZ, composition and download commands contextually without opening another workflow or changing records. Modern application controls retain existing ownership. Preserve Settings/About return context and unsent input, normal disconnect/reconnect behavior and existing reset/restore safeguards. Add no Gopher network transport, endpoint entry, persistence/schema change, model work or browser download action. Ordinary session/history recording may continue.

5. **Evidence and product disclosure.** Update README, the existing historical research record and discoverable About content with source URLs, access dates, historical scope, confidence, original-content authorship, accepted category D choices and unresolved host/client route. Briefly identify the bundled local example without crowding routine menus with research detail. Do not claim live retrieval, complete historical coverage or protocol conformance. Keep Archie, host paging and graphical-client reconstruction outside this Issue.

6. **Coordinator validation using existing tooling.** Add focused controller and production-browser checks for both entry parents; nested and search-result returns; repeated selection; replacement queries; zero results; malformed input; service isolation; MAIN/re-entry; and connection forwarding. Exercise an anonymous restored-empty world and a registered world, Settings/About return, a 320px keyboard journey, simulated IME submission, and literal Japanese/spacing/markup in documents and exported terminal logs. Compare protected members/SIGs/forums/posts/mail/read-state/settings before and after, including JSON export; allow normal session/history changes. Confirm browsing does not seed missing imported records or introduce external/model requests, workers or popups with AI disabled.

7. **Preserve existing regressions.** Run relevant existing Internet/navigation, functional, storage, consent, composition, IME and terminal checks, then the existing complete suite through `npm test -- --workers=3`, which includes configured TypeScript checking and production build. Record actual commands/results, failures, corrections and skipped checks. Preserve behavioral assertions; change obsolete expectations only where selector 4 legitimately changes the Internet directory. Review the final diff, documentation links/anchors and `git diff --check`. Three-worker success must not be reported as resolving default-worker reliability.

## Optional validation

Native Japanese IME, additional browser engines and additional historical-user feedback may supplement automated evidence. They are not completion gates. No real-model or hardware validation is needed for this bundled service.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. The Coordinator should record pre-merge results; this Issue adds no separate post-merge test or deployment-verification requirement.
